The list of executives is still being reviewed and could change. Xi’s chief of staff, Cai Qi, is among senior officials reviewing potential participants for the September 24 state visit, the report said.

The possible inclusion of Wang would come against significant trade barriers facing Chinese electric-vehicle makers in the U.S. The United States has imposed 100% tariffs on Chinese EVs, while the Pentagon in June blacklisted BYD
over alleged links to China’s People’s Liberation Army. BYD
has denied supporting the Chinese military.
According to the people, potential U.S. business deals, loyalty to the Communist Party, and the ability of executives to avoid overshadowing Xi are among the considerations for selecting delegates.

The report said any potential arrangement allowing Chinese automakers to manufacture vehicles in the U.S. could become part of broader discussions during Xi’s visit. Trump has said he would be open to Chinese carmakers establishing U.S. plants using American workers.

title: China weighs BYD CEO for business delegation at Xi-Trump summit
